positions.name: Corning Incorporated
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Thu 9/17 at the close, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Dilution overreaction: GLW fell 13.7% Mon 9/14 (worst S&P 500 performer) on a $2B at-the-market equity program with Goldman Sachs - roughly 1.6% of its $124B market cap. It recovered +1.1% after hours and is +1.3% in 9/15 pre-market.
positions.risks: The AI-infrastructure de-rating that also hit MACOM (-11.3%), Teradyne (-11.2%) and Coherent (-10.0%) on Monday is a separate, live headwind, and ATM programs print supply into every rally. GLW had run ~91% YTD before this.

positions.name: RTX Corp.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Thu 9/17 at the close, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: The DoD Lead Inspector General report to Congress, released Mon 9/14, documents munitions inventory shortfalls and industrial-base bottlenecks from the $33.4B Iran war. Trump separately named RTX's Tomahawk, Standard Missile and Patriot lines on Truth Social. Follows Raytheon's $22.9B August Tomahawk award.

positions.name: Aon Plc
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Thu 9/17 at the close, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Commenced a seven-tranche US investment-grade debt sale Mon 9/14 to fund the planned $17B acquisition of USI Insurance Services from KKR. Shares rose 2.3% on the day while XLF fell 0.5% and BAC dropped 5.1% - financing progress de-risks the deal.

positions.name: CME Group, Inc.
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat immediately after the Wed 9/16 FOMC statement and dot plot, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Fed-meeting volume trade: the FOMC's two-day meeting opens 9/15 with CME FedWatch pricing a 94.5% chance of the first rate hike since 2023, plus a fresh dot plot. The 10-year crossed 5% Monday for the first time since 2023 (highest close since 2007) - CME's rate complex is where that repricing gets hedged.
positions.risks: Volume converts to revenue with a lag, and the stock can fall on a hawkish risk-off day even as volumes spike. The 25bp hike is already 94.5% priced, so only the dot plot is a real surprise.

positions.name: MetLife, Inc.
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat immediately after the Wed 9/16 FOMC statement and dot plot, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Rate-hike beneficiary into Wednesday: the 10-year hit 5.01% intraday Monday, its highest close since 2007, lifting reinvestment yields on MetLife's spread-based Retirement and Income Solutions book. UBS expects the dot plot to signal a further hike this year.
positions.risks: No 9/15 pre-market print existed, so the entry is marked at Monday's $97.75 official close - execution slippage is possible. A dovish dot plot flattens the curve and reverses the trade, and credit losses rise if higher rates crack the economy.

positions.name: Intel Corporation
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on confirmation OR denial of an SK Hynix arrangement at the Ohio site, on the Fri 9/18 close at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Two stacked catalysts inside 3.5 hours. Reuters reported at 03:22 ET on 9/16 that SK Hynix is in exploratory talks with Intel to make memory chips in the US for the first time - either leasing part of Intel's long-delayed Ohio complex or forming a JV with Intel and cloud providers hunting memory supply; SK Hynix confirmed it is 'reviewing various measures' but that nothing is decided. Then at 06:29 ET Tigress Financial raised its Intel price target to $145 from $118, keeping Buy, versus a FactSet mean PT of $121.11. INTC printed 99.81 in pre-market against a 97.14 close, +2.75%.
positions.risks: Both companies have publicly hedged: Intel called it 'speculation', SK Hynix denied an Ohio acquisition outright back in July, and Seoul can block anything touching 'national core technology' under the Industrial Technology Protection Act. The Ohio fabs are not due until 2030-31, so nothing here changes 2027 earnings. Trailing P/E is negative and the stock has quadrupled off a $24.45 52-week low.
positions.driver: Tier 1 - discrete named report + analyst action

positions.name: Qorvo, Inc.
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on a SAMR clearance headline or any re-widening of the merger-arb spread, on the Fri 9/18 close at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: CEO Phil Brace told a Goldman Sachs conference last week that the $22B all-stock Skyworks/Qorvo combination has entered its final regulatory stage, with China's SAMR review targeting a year-end close. The arb spread has been compressing on that: SWKS +28.1% last week (best since 2009) and +10.5% Tuesday, QRVO +7.4% Tuesday to a 118.06 close. QRVO printed 119.59 pre-market 9/16, +1.30%.
positions.risks: Entering 0.8% below a 52-week high of $120.52 set 9/11, with RSI flagged at 84.9 on 9/14 - textbook overbought. SAMR is the one regulator that can still kill or delay this, and a China headline cuts both ways. Taking the target rather than the acquirer means the position is short the deal break.

positions.name: Coherent Corp.
positions.exitRule: Intraday - flat by the 9/16 close, ahead of the 2:00pm ET FOMC statement
positions.catalyst: Largest pre-market gain of any liquid large-cap on the board: 279.80 versus a 271.17 close, +3.18%. Coherent was -7.4% Monday in the AI-doomerism selloff triggered by the Amodei/Altman/Musk 'pace the frontier' essays. That narrative reversed at the All-In Summit, where Broadcom's Hock Tan confirmed 2027/2028 guidance is untouched by slowdown talk, and Gabelli PM Hendi Susanto named next-generation optical connectivity as the highest-convexity way to buy the dip.
positions.risks: Highest-beta name in today's book and 36% below a $440 52-week high, so the downtrend is intact. A 64x trailing P/E is the most rate-sensitive multiple here with the 10-year at 5.005%. Intraday-only for exactly this reason - no FOMC and no overnight gap.

positions.name: FTAI Aviation Ltd.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Fri 9/18 at the close, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Announced a $500 million share repurchase program; the stock printed 181.06 pre-market versus a 176.44 close, +2.62%. Against a $18.1B market cap the authorisation is ~2.8% of shares, and it lands with the stock 44% below its $323.51 February 52-week high.
positions.risks: A buyback authorisation is not a buyback - nothing obliges FTAI to execute. The stock is down 44% from its high for reasons the announcement does not address, and jet fuel running ~70% above 2025 with carriers cutting routes pressures the leasing and aftermarket engine business directly. 44.7x book is expensive for an asset lessor.

positions.name: Vertiv Holdings Co
positions.exitRule: Intraday - flat by the 9/16 close, ahead of the 2:00pm ET FOMC statement

The reversal has a named cause: AI-doomerism cooled at the All-In Summit, Broadcom's Hock Tan reaffirmed 2027/2028 guidance, and BofA's Vivek Arya published a 9/14 note calling the controversy 'noise' against AI capex tripling to $3tn+ by decade-end, with AI network capacity running near 100% utilisation and rental prices rising even on older accelerators.
positions.risks: 37% below a $379.94 May high at 19.2x book and 53.7x earnings - a de-rating that has not finished de-rating. Citi separately flagged AI-safety concerns as a specific drag on data-centre names. Intraday only: no FOMC exposure.

positions.name: Eaton Corp. plc
positions.exitRule: Intraday - flat by the 9/16 close, ahead of the 2:00pm ET FOMC statement
positions.catalyst: Same electrical/data-centre power reversal, lower beta: ETN was -5.8% Monday in the AI-capex selloff and prints 396.54 pre-market versus a 392.40 close, +1.06%. Sits 17% below its $478 August 52-week high - far less broken than VRT or COHR.
positions.risks: The most crowded 'picks and shovels' trade in Industrials at 40x earnings, and a 1.06% pre-market bid is the weakest confirmation of the three dislocation-reversal names. Non-data-centre end markets (vehicle, eMobility, commercial construction) are directly hurt by a 5% 10-year. Intraday only.

positions.name: Constellation Energy Corporation

positions.name: Vistra Corp.

positions.name: Newmont Corporation
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the Thu 9/17 open, after the FOMC statement and dot plot are digested
positions.catalyst: Deliberate FOMC-day expression, and the only position in the book held through the 2:00pm statement by design. A 25bp hike to 4.00% is 92.5% priced on CME FedWatch, and gold has already paid for it - down 2.8% over the past month into a six-week low. This morning gold spot is +0.88% at ~$4,331.85 with GLD +1.02% and SLV +1.36% while the dollar index is barely changed, which is a real-rate bid rather than an inflation hedge. NEM prints 126.00 pre-market versus a 124.19 close, +1.46%.
positions.risks: Holding a rate-sensitive asset straight through the single largest scheduled event of the week is the whole trade and also the whole risk: a hawkish dot plot signalling more than one further hike sends real rates up and gold down hard. NEM is also within 6.9% of a $135.29 52-week high, so there is little valuation cushion.

positions.name: Agnico Eagle Mines Limited
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the Thu 9/17 open, after the FOMC statement and dot plot are digested
positions.catalyst: Same pre-FOMC gold expression, higher-quality operator. AEM prints 199.96 pre-market versus a 196.90 close, +1.55% - stronger confirmation than NEM - and trades at 16.8x earnings with a 21.6% gap still open to its $255.24 March 52-week high.
positions.risks: Identical FOMC risk to NEM and NEM/AEM/WPM are one correlated bet on the dot plot, not three. AEM is up 48.8% from its $134.38 July low. A hawkish surprise hits all three simultaneously; sizing assumes that and the trio is capped at three names inside the four-per-sector limit.

positions.name: Wheaton Precious Metals Corp.
positions.exitRule: Overnight (next-day open) - flat on the Thu 9/17 open, after the FOMC statement and dot plot are digested
positions.catalyst: Strongest pre-market confirmation of the three precious-metals names: 153.79 versus a 150.02 close, +2.51%. A streaming/royalty model rather than a miner, so it carries gold price leverage without operating cost exposure to the diesel shock now running at a record $6.26/gal - the input that is crushing conventional mining margins.
positions.risks: 33.1x earnings and 7.0x book is the most expensive way to own gold here, and the stock is 7.2% below a $165.76 March high. Streams are long-duration cash flows, which makes WPM the most duration-sensitive of the trio if the dot plot is hawkish. Held through the FOMC by design.

positions.name: TORM plc
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on a formal Hafnia offer or any disclosure that the stake has stopped growing, on the Fri 9/18 close at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Hafnia raised its TORM holding to 18.22% on 9/16 after buying another 4.5 million shares - a named strategic acquirer accumulating toward a control position in product tankers, the sector with the single best fundamental backdrop on the board. TRMD prints 35.99 pre-market versus a 34.93 close, +3.03%, on 8.4m shares traded Tuesday against a 1.3m 30-day average. Diesel at a record $6.26/gal and Saudi Aramco cancelling European cargoes is what the freight rates are actually pricing.
positions.risks: Entry is 0.14% above the $35.938 52-week high set 9/9, so there is no overhead supply and no reference level under the trade. An 18.22% stake is not an offer and Hafnia has made no bid; stake-building can stall for quarters. The $3.58B market cap is the smallest in the book and it went ex-dividend $2.40 on 9/10, so the tape is still digesting that. UK-domiciled operator listed in the US.
positions.driver: Tier 1 - stake accumulation by a named strategic buyer
